summary: John Victor Boulton (1934–2006) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at SOAS University of London (~1963–1967). He served at SOAS as a Lecturer in Bengali and Oriya from 1962 to 1988.

John Vincent Bellezza (b. 1957) is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel, and held a post attested in 2014 at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

John W. Pettit is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College and doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, also studying under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

John W. Schroeder (b. 1962) specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon (Ph.D. under Don Levi). He taught at Oregon, the College of Wooster, and St. Mary's College of Maryland.

John W. Spellman (1934–2021) was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1958–1961). He taught at the University of Washington (~1964–1966) and served as Professor at the University of Windsor (~1967–1999).

John Watson McCrindle (1825–1913) was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Edinburgh. His career included serving as Principal of Doveton College (1859), Professor at Krishnagar Government College (1866), and Principal of Patna College (1867–1880).
John Wenger (1811–1880) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Bern in 1827 and at the University of Rhode Island, receiving a D.D. in ~1878.

John Whalen-Bridge (b. 1961) works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at the University of Connecticut, UC Davis, and USC (Ph.D. 1992), he served at the University of the Ryukyus (1993–1998) and became Associate Professor at the National University of Singapore (1998).

John Whaley Watson (1838–1889) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Bombay Staff Corps (~1861–1889), as President of the Rajasthik Court in Kathiawar (~1873–1886), and as political agent for the Kathiawar Agency (1881–1889).

John William Neill was an Indologist who studied at King's College London and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Professor of Indian Law and Lecturer in Marathi at University College London (1896–1917) and Reader of Marathi at SOAS.

John Wilson (1804–1875) was an Indologist and linguist educated at the University of Edinburgh. He served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, founded Wilson College, Mumbai, and was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1868).
John Zephaniah Holwell (1711–1798) was an Indologist who studied surgery at Guy's Hospital (~1729–1732). He became a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1767.

Join Saeki (1867–1952) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji and under Jōchō Chihaya. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1928), the Japan Academy (1929), Kangakuin, and served as chief abbot at Horyu-ji (1903–1950).
Joji Fujii (b. 1947) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He completed his studies at Kyoto University (~1966–1974) and subsequently held an academic post there from ~1989 to 2012.

Jokai Hiraoka (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo (~1944–1950), and held professorial posts at Shuchiin University and Otemae University (~1966–1994).

Jon Holt specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. in Japanese from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1993–1995) and a Ph.D. from the University of Washington, becoming Professor of Japanese at Portland State University in 2010.

Jon Kabat-Zinn (b. 1944) works in religious studies and medicine. Educated at Haverford College and MIT (Ph.D. ~1964–1971), he studied under various teachers and served at the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School (~1979–2000), where he founded the Stress Reduction Clinic.

Jonardon Ganeri (b. 1963) is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford (D.Phil. under Bimal Krishna Matilal). He has held posts at Nottingham, Clare Hall Cambridge, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, NYU, and the University of Toronto.

Jonathan A. Silk (b. 1960) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who earned his doctorate at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. His academic posts include Yale University (1998–2002), UCLA (~2002–2007), and Leiden University (2007).

Jonathan C. Gold (b. 1969) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion. Educated at Amherst College and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. 2003), he taught at the University of Vermont, Drew University, and Princeton University (2008).
